title: Trie (Prefix Tree)
tagline: A tree of characters for O(L) insert/search and lightning-fast prefix queries.

intuition.analogy: A physical index where words sharing a prefix share a path: all words starting 'ca' branch off the same 'c→a' corridor. To check if 'cat' exists, you just walk c→a→t.
paragraphs: A trie stores strings as paths in a tree where each edge is a character. Words with common prefixes share the upper part of their paths, making prefix operations extremely natural and fast.
Insertion and lookup take O(L) where L is the word length — independent of how many words are stored. A boolean flag at a node marks the end of a complete word.

Tries power autocomplete, spell-checkers, IP routing, and 'maximum XOR' problems (a binary trie over bits). They trade memory for speed: storing all prefixes explicitly enables instant prefix matching.
intuition.keyIdea: Shared prefixes share paths; walking L edges inserts or finds a word regardless of dictionary size.

steps.title: Node structure
steps.detail: Each node has child pointers (one per alphabet symbol) and an isEnd flag.

steps.title: Insert
steps.detail: Walk down character by character, creating missing child nodes; mark isEnd at the final node.

steps.title: Search / startsWith
steps.detail: Walk the path; search succeeds if the final node has isEnd, prefix-check succeeds if the path merely exists.

complexity.timeReason: One step per character of the word.
complexity.spaceReason: Each node may hold an array of child pointers.

pitfalls: Array-of-26 children wastes memory for sparse alphabets — use a hash map for large/unicode alphabets.
Remember to free nodes (C++) or you leak memory.

dryRun.clickMoment: 'car' and 'card' share the entire c→a→r path — only the final 'd' is new. The trie automatically deduplicates shared prefixes, which is exactly what makes prefix queries instant.

approach: A trie node has up to 26 children and an end-of-word flag. insert/search/startsWith all walk the tree letter by letter.

problems.title: Word Search II
problems.statement: Find all dictionary words on a board.
problems.hint: Build a trie of words, DFS the board with pruning.

approach: Insert all words into a trie, then DFS the grid once, descending the trie in lockstep with the path.
When a trie node marks a complete word, record it (and clear it to avoid duplicates). The trie prunes impossible directions early.

problems.title: Add and Search Word
problems.hint: Trie with branching DFS on wildcards.

approach: Insert words into a trie. For search, '.' matches any child, so the search branches at dots — handle it with recursion (or DFS).
At a '.', recurse into every existing child; otherwise follow the single matching edge.

problems.title: Maximum XOR of Two Numbers
problems.statement: Max XOR pair in an array.
problems.hint: Binary trie over bits; greedily pick opposite bits.

approach: Insert each number's 32-bit binary into a binary trie (bit 0/1 children). To maximise XOR with a number, greedily pick the opposite bit at each level.
For every number, traverse the trie choosing the complementary bit when possible; track the best XOR.

problems.title: Replace Words
problems.statement: Replace words by their shortest dictionary root.
problems.hint: Trie of roots; match the shortest prefix.

approach: Insert all roots into a trie. For each word, walk the trie until the first end-of-root and replace the word with that shortest root.
If no root matches, keep the original word.
